qns_content.text: What is the major product when pentan-2-ol is dehydrated with conc. \( \ce{H2SO4} \)?

text_solutions: Dehydration of pentan-2-ol gives a mixture of alkenes, with pent-2-ene as the major product according to Saytzeff’s rule.

qns_content.text: What is the product when 2-methylpropan-1-ol is oxidized with PCC?

text_solutions: 2-Methylpropan-1-ol (\( \ce{(CH3)2CHCH2OH} \)), a primary alcohol, is oxidized to 2-methylpropanal (\( \ce{(CH3)2CHCHO} \)) with PCC, stopping at the aldehyde.

qns_content.text: What is the product when 2-methylpropan-1-ol is oxidized with \( \ce{KMnO4} \)?

text_solutions: 2-Methylpropan-1-ol (\( \ce{(CH3)2CHCH2OH} \)), a primary alcohol, is oxidized to 2-methylpropanoic acid (\( \ce{(CH3)2CHCOOH} \)) with \( \ce{KMnO4} \), a strong oxidant.

qns_content.text: What is observed when phenol reacts with \( \ce{Br2} \) in water?

text_solutions: Phenol reacts with \( \ce{Br2} \) in water to form a white precipitate of 2,4,6-tribromophenol due to the strong activation of the ring by the -OH group.

qns_content.text: Which compound is formed when benzyl alcohol reacts with \( \ce{KMnO4} \)?

text_solutions: Benzyl alcohol (\( \ce{C6H5CH2OH} \)), a primary alcohol, is oxidized to benzoic acid (\( \ce{C6H5COOH} \)) with \( \ce{KMnO4} \), a strong oxidizing agent.

qns_content.text: Which reagent converts propene to propan-2-ol following Markovnikov’s rule?

text_solutions: Acid-catalyzed hydration follows Markovnikov’s rule, giving propan-2-ol. Hydroboration-oxidation gives propan-1-ol (anti-Markovnikov).

qns_content.text: Which alcohol produces 2-methylpropanal on oxidation with PCC?

text_solutions: 2-Methylpropan-1-ol (\( \ce{(CH3)2CHCH2OH} \)), a primary alcohol, oxidizes to 2-methylpropanal (\( \ce{(CH3)2CHCHO} \)) with PCC.

qns_content.text: Which reagent is used to oxidize a primary alcohol to an aldehyde without further oxidation?

text_solutions: Pyridinium chlorochromate (PCC) selectively oxidizes primary alcohols to aldehydes without converting them to carboxylic acids.

qns_content.text: What is the product when phenol reacts with \( \ce{CHCl3} \) and \( \ce{NaOH} \) followed by acidification?

text_solutions: In the Reimer-Tiemann reaction, phenol reacts with \( \ce{CHCl3} \) and \( \ce{NaOH} \) to form salicylaldehyde (2-hydroxybenzaldehyde) after acidification.

qns_content.text: Which reagent reduces acetophenone to 1-phenylethanol?

text_solutions: Acetophenone (\( \ce{C6H5COCH3} \)) is reduced to 1-phenylethanol (\( \ce{C6H5CH(OH)CH3} \)) using \( \ce{NaBH4} \), a selective reducing agent for ketones.

qns_content.text: What is the product when benzyl alcohol is oxidized with \( \ce{KMnO4} \)?

text_solutions: Benzyl alcohol is oxidized by strong oxidizing agents like \( \ce{KMnO4} \) to benzoic acid.

qns_content.text: What is the major product of acid dehydration of butan-2-ol?

text_solutions: Dehydration of butan-2-ol gives a mixture of alkenes, with but-2-ene as the major product according to Saytzeff’s rule.

qns_content.text: What is the IUPAC name of \( \ce{CH3-CH2-CH(OH)-CH2-OH} \)?

text_solutions: The compound has a 4-carbon chain with -OH groups on carbons 1 and 3, named butane-1,3-diol in IUPAC nomenclature.

qns_content.text: Which alcohol has the highest solubility in water among the following?

text_solutions: Propane-1,2-diol (\( \ce{CH3CH(OH)CH2OH} \)) has two -OH groups, enhancing hydrogen bonding with water, making it more soluble than monohydric alcohols like propan-1-ol.

qns_content.text: What is the common name of \( \ce{CH3CH(OH)CH2OH} \)?

text_solutions: \( \ce{CH3CH(OH)CH2OH} \) (propane-1,2-diol) is commonly known as propylene glycol, a widely used diol.

qns_content.text: Which alcohol is produced by the acid-catalyzed hydration of 1-butene?

text_solutions: 1-Butene (\( \ce{CH2=CH-CH2-CH3} \)) undergoes acid-catalyzed hydration with \( \ce{H2SO4} \) and \( \ce{H2O} \), following Markovnikov’s rule, to form butan-2-ol (\( \ce{CH3CH(OH)CH2CH3} \)).

qns_content.text: What is the IUPAC name of the compound \( \ce{CH3-CH(OH)-CH2-CH3} \)?

text_solutions: The longest chain containing the -OH group has 4 carbons, so the base name is butane. The -OH is on the second carbon from the end nearest to it, so it is butan-2-ol.

qns_content.text: Which reagent produces a ketone from a secondary alcohol without forming an acid?

text_solutions: PCC oxidizes secondary alcohols to ketones selectively, stopping at the ketone stage without further oxidation to a carboxylic acid.

qns_content.text: What is the IUPAC name of \( \ce{CH3-CH(OH)-CH2-CH2-OH} \)?

text_solutions: The compound has a 4-carbon chain with -OH groups on carbons 1 and 3, named butane-1,3-diol in IUPAC nomenclature.

qns_content.text: How is 2-methylpropan-2-ol synthesized from methyl magnesium bromide?

text_solutions: Methyl magnesium bromide (\( \ce{CH3MgBr} \)) reacts with acetone (\( \ce{CH3COCH3} \)), adding the methyl group to the carbonyl carbon, and hydrolysis yields 2-methylpropan-2-ol (\( \ce{(CH3)3COH} \)).

qns_content.text: What is the reagent used to convert butan-2-one to butan-2-ol?

text_solutions: Butan-2-one (\( \ce{CH3-CO-CH2-CH3} \)) is reduced to butan-2-ol (\( \ce{CH3-CH(OH)-CH2-CH3} \)) using a reducing agent like \( \ce{NaBH4} \), which selectively reduces ketones to secondary alcohols.

qns_content.text: The reaction of phenol with \( \ce{CO2} \) and \( \ce{NaOH} \) at high pressure and temperature yields which product?

text_solutions: In Kolbe’s reaction, phenol reacts with \( \ce{CO2} \) and \( \ce{NaOH} \) under heat and pressure, followed by acidification, to form salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid).

qns_content.text: Which reaction condition converts cyclohexanol to cyclohexene?

text_solutions: Cyclohexanol dehydrates to cyclohexene with conc. \( \ce{H2SO4} \) at 160°C via an E1 mechanism, eliminating water.

qns_content.text: What is the product when phenol reacts with \( \ce{NaOH} \) and \( \ce{CHCl3} \) followed by acidification?

text_solutions: In the Reimer-Tiemann reaction, phenol reacts with \( \ce{CHCl3} \) and \( \ce{NaOH} \) to form salicylaldehyde (\( \ce{C6H4(OH)CHO} \)) after acidification.

qns_content.text: The major product of dehydration of butan-1-ol with conc. \( \ce{H2SO4} \) at 170°C is:

text_solutions: Primary alcohols undergo dehydration to give mainly terminal alkenes like but-1-ene.

qns_content.text: Which compound is produced when phenol reacts with \( \ce{Na} \) at room temperature?

text_solutions: Phenol (\( \ce{C6H5OH} \)) reacts with \( \ce{Na} \) to form sodium phenoxide (\( \ce{C6H5ONa} \)) and \( \ce{H2} \) gas, showcasing its acidic nature.

qns_content.text: Which of the following compounds reacts most vigorously with sodium metal?

text_solutions: Phenol is more acidic than alcohols due to resonance stabilization of the phenoxide ion, so it reacts more vigorously with sodium metal.

qns_content.text: What is the IUPAC name of \( \ce{CH3-CH(OH)-CH2-CH2-CH3} \)?

text_solutions: The compound has a 5-carbon chain with the -OH on the second carbon from the end nearest to it, named pentan-2-ol.

qns_content.text: Which alcohol produces a tertiary carbocation as an intermediate during dehydration with conc. \( \ce{H2SO4} \)?

text_solutions: 2-Methylpropan-2-ol (\( \ce{(CH3)3COH} \)), a tertiary alcohol, forms a stable tertiary carbocation (\( \ce{(CH3)3C+} \)) during dehydration via an E1 mechanism.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is an allylic alcohol?

text_solutions: An allylic alcohol has the -OH group on a carbon adjacent to a double bond. \( \ce{CH2=CH-CH2OH} \) (allyl alcohol) fits this definition.

qns_content.text: Which alcohol, when treated with Lucas reagent, shows turbidity within 5–10 minutes?

text_solutions: Propan-2-ol (\( \ce{CH3CH(OH)CH3} \)), a secondary alcohol, forms a secondary carbocation with Lucas reagent (\( \ce{ZnCl2} \) in conc. \( \ce{HCl} \)), causing turbidity in 5–10 minutes.

qns_content.text: What is the maximum number of carbon atoms in the longest chain of \( \ce{CH3-C(OH)(CH3)-CH2-CH3} \)?

text_solutions: The longest chain in \( \ce{CH3-C(OH)(CH3)-CH2-CH3} \) (2-methylbutan-2-ol) includes four carbons: \( \ce{CH3-CH2-C(OH)-CH3} \), with -OH and a methyl branch on the second carbon.

qns_content.text: What is the product of the Reimer-Tiemann reaction with phenol?

text_solutions: Phenol reacts with \( \ce{CHCl3} \) and aqueous \( \ce{NaOH} \) in the Reimer-Tiemann reaction to form salicylaldehyde (2-hydroxybenzaldehyde) via electrophilic substitution at the ortho position.

qns_content.text: Which alcohol is produced when ethyl magnesium bromide reacts with ethanal followed by hydrolysis?

text_solutions: Ethyl magnesium bromide (\( \ce{CH3CH2MgBr} \)) reacts with ethanal (\( \ce{CH3CHO} \)), adding the ethyl group to the carbonyl, yielding butan-2-ol (\( \ce{CH3CH(OH)CH2CH3} \)) after hydrolysis.

qns_content.text: Which alcohol is produced when methyl magnesium bromide reacts with butanal followed by hydrolysis?

text_solutions: Methyl magnesium bromide (\( \ce{CH3MgBr} \)) reacts with butanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CHO} \)), adding the methyl group to the carbonyl, yielding pentan-2-ol (\( \ce{CH3CH(OH)CH2CH2CH3} \)) after hydrolysis.

qns_content.text: Which alcohol is most commonly used as a solvent in pharmaceutical preparations?

text_solutions: Ethanol is the most commonly used solvent in pharmaceutical preparations due to its effectiveness and relatively low toxicity.

qns_content.text: Which alcohol is produced when ethyl magnesium bromide reacts with propanal followed by hydrolysis?

text_solutions: Ethyl magnesium bromide (\( \ce{CH3CH2MgBr} \)) reacts with propanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CHO} \)), adding the ethyl group to the carbonyl, yielding pentan-3-ol (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH(OH)CH2CH3} \)) after hydrolysis.

qns_content.text: What is the product when phenol reacts with \( \ce{Br2} \) in water?

text_solutions: Phenol reacts with \( \ce{Br2} \) in water to form 2,4,6-tribromophenol due to the strong activation of the ring by the -OH group, leading to trisubstitution.

qns_content.text: Which compound is formed when 2-methylpropan-2-ol is dehydrated?

text_solutions: 2-Methylpropan-2-ol (\( \ce{(CH3)3COH} \)) dehydrates with conc. \( \ce{H2SO4} \) to form 2-methylpropene (\( \ce{CH2=C(CH3)CH3} \)), following Saytzeff’s rule.

qns_content.text: Which reagent confirms the presence of a phenolic -OH group in a compound?

text_solutions: Neutral \( \ce{FeCl3} \) forms a violet complex with phenols due to coordination with the phenoxide ion, distinguishing them from alcohols.

qns_content.text: Which phenol derivative is used as an explosive?

text_solutions: 2,4,6-Trinitrophenol (picric acid), formed by nitrating phenol with conc. \( \ce{HNO3} \), is used as an explosive due to its high reactivity.

qns_content.text: Which compound is produced when phenol reacts with conc. \( \ce{HNO3} \) at 60°C?

text_solutions: Phenol reacts with conc. \( \ce{HNO3} \) at 60°C to form 2,4,6-trinitrophenol (picric acid) due to the strong activation of the ring by the -OH group, allowing trisubstitution.

qns_content.text: What is the product when propan-1-ol is oxidized with alkaline \( \ce{KMnO4} \)?

text_solutions: Propan-1-ol (\( \ce{CH3-CH2-CH2OH} \)), a primary alcohol, is oxidized to propanoic acid (\( \ce{CH3-CH2-COOH} \)) with a strong oxidizing agent like alkaline \( \ce{KMnO4} \).

qns_content.text: Which alcohol produces propanal on oxidation with PCC?

text_solutions: Propan-1-ol (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2OH} \)), a primary alcohol, oxidizes to propanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CHO} \)) with PCC.

qns_content.text: Phenol reacts with chloroform in the presence of aqueous \( \ce{NaOH} \) to produce which compound?

text_solutions: This is the Reimer-Tiemann reaction, where phenol reacts with \( \ce{CHCl3} \) and \( \ce{NaOH} \) to form salicylaldehyde (2-hydroxybenzaldehyde) via ortho substitution.

qns_content.text: What is the product when 2-methylbutan-2-ol reacts with Lucas reagent?

text_solutions: 2-Methylbutan-2-ol (\( \ce{CH3C(OH)(CH3)CH2CH3} \)), a tertiary alcohol, reacts with Lucas reagent (\( \ce{ZnCl2} \) in conc. \( \ce{HCl} \)) to form 2-chloro-2-methylbutane (\( \ce{CH3C(Cl)(CH3)CH2CH3} \)) via an \( \ce{S_N1} \) mechanism.

qns_content.text: Which factor explains the lower boiling point of methanol compared to ethanol?

text_solutions: Methanol (\( \ce{CH3OH} \)) has a lower molecular weight (32 g/mol) than ethanol (\( \ce{CH3CH2OH} \), 46 g/mol), reducing van der Waals forces and thus lowering its boiling point.

qns_content.text: Which alcohol is produced by the acid-catalyzed hydration of 2-methylpropene?

text_solutions: 2-Methylpropene (\( \ce{CH2=C(CH3)CH3} \)) undergoes acid-catalyzed hydration with \( \ce{H2SO4} \) and \( \ce{H2O} \), following Markovnikov’s rule, to form 2-methylpropan-2-ol (\( \ce{(CH3)3COH} \)).

qns_content.text: Which compound is formed when ethanol reacts with \( \ce{I2} \) and \( \ce{NaOH} \)?

text_solutions: Ethanol (\( \ce{CH3CH2OH} \)) oxidizes to acetaldehyde, which reacts with \( \ce{I2} \) and \( \ce{NaOH} \) in the iodoform test to form iodoform (\( \ce{CHI3} \)), a yellow precipitate.

qns_content.text: Which reagent oxidizes benzyl alcohol to benzoic acid?

text_solutions: Benzyl alcohol (\( \ce{C6H5CH2OH} \)) is oxidized to benzoic acid (\( \ce{C6H5COOH} \)) using a strong oxidizing agent like \( \ce{KMnO4} \) in alkaline conditions.

qns_content.text: How is benzyl alcohol synthesized from benzyl chloride?

text_solutions: Benzyl chloride (\( \ce{C6H5CH2Cl} \)) undergoes nucleophilic substitution with aqueous \( \ce{NaOH} \) to replace -Cl with -OH, forming benzyl alcohol (\( \ce{C6H5CH2OH} \)).

qns_content.text: Why does ethanol have a higher boiling point than methoxymethane?

text_solutions: Ethanol (\( \ce{CH3CH2OH} \)) forms hydrogen bonds due to the -OH group, requiring more energy to break, whereas methoxymethane (\( \ce{CH3OCH3} \)) lacks hydrogen bonding, leading to a lower boiling point.

qns_content.text: What is the IUPAC name of \( \ce{CH3-CH2-CH2-CH(OH)-CH3} \)?

text_solutions: The compound has a 5-carbon chain with the -OH on the second carbon from the end nearest to it, named pentan-2-ol.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a benzylic alcohol?

text_solutions: A benzylic alcohol has the -OH group on a carbon directly attached to a benzene ring. \( \ce{C6H5CH2OH} \) (benzyl alcohol) fits this definition.

qns_content.text: What is the product when phenol reacts with conc. \( \ce{HNO3} \)?

text_solutions: Phenol reacts with conc. \( \ce{HNO3} \) to form 2,4,6-trinitrophenol (picric acid) due to the strong activation of the ring by the -OH group, allowing trisubstitution.

qns_content.text: Which reagent is used to oxidize a primary alcohol to a carboxylic acid?

text_solutions: Primary alcohols are oxidized to carboxylic acids using strong oxidizing agents like alkaline \( \ce{KMnO4} \), which fully oxidizes the alcohol through the aldehyde stage.

qns_content.text: Which reagent is used to convert cyclohexanol to cyclohexanone?

text_solutions: Cyclohexanol, a secondary alcohol, is oxidized to cyclohexanone with PCC, which selectively oxidizes secondary alcohols to ketones.

qns_content.text: Which alcohol yields 2-methylbut-2-ene as the major product on dehydration with conc. \( \ce{H2SO4} \)?

text_solutions: 2-Methylbutan-2-ol (\( \ce{CH3C(OH)(CH3)CH2CH3} \)) dehydrates to 2-methylbut-2-ene (\( \ce{CH3C(CH3)=CHCH3} \)) as the major product, following Saytzeff’s rule.

qns_content.text: Which alcohol produces butan-2-one upon oxidation?

text_solutions: Butan-2-ol (\( \ce{CH3CH(OH)CH2CH3} \)), a secondary alcohol, oxidizes to butan-2-one (\( \ce{CH3COCH2CH3} \)) with reagents like PCC or \( \ce{CrO3} \).

qns_content.text: What is the product when propan-1-ol reacts with excess conc. \( \ce{H2SO4} \) at 140°C?

text_solutions: At 140°C, propan-1-ol undergoes intermolecular dehydration in the presence of conc. \( \ce{H2SO4} \) to form di-n-propyl ether (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2-O-CH2CH2CH3} \)). Alkene formation occurs at higher temperature (~170°C).

qns_content.text: Which compound is produced when ethyl magnesium chloride reacts with formaldehyde followed by hydrolysis?

text_solutions: Ethyl magnesium chloride (\( \ce{CH3CH2MgCl} \)) reacts with formaldehyde (\( \ce{HCHO} \)), adding the ethyl group to the carbonyl carbon, and hydrolysis yields propan-1-ol (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2OH} \)).

qns_content.text: Which compound is formed when phenol reacts with dilute \( \ce{HNO3} \)?

text_solutions: Phenol reacts with dilute \( \ce{HNO3} \) to form a mixture of 2-nitrophenol and 4-nitrophenol, with 2-nitrophenol being a significant product due to ortho-para directing effect of -OH.

qns_content.text: Which alcohol yields pent-2-ene as the major product on dehydration with conc. \( \ce{H2SO4} \) at 160°C?

text_solutions: Pentan-2-ol (\( \ce{CH3CH(OH)CH2CH2CH3} \)) dehydrates to pent-2-ene (\( \ce{CH3CH=CHCH2CH3} \)) as the major product, following Saytzeff’s rule.

qns_content.text: The dehydration of ethanol to ethene proceeds via which type of mechanism?

text_solutions: Ethanol, a primary alcohol, undergoes acid-catalyzed dehydration via a concerted E2 mechanism because formation of a primary carbocation is unstable.

qns_content.text: Which compound is formed when phenol reacts with \( \ce{Na} \)?

text_solutions: Phenol (\( \ce{C6H5OH} \)) reacts with sodium metal to form sodium phenoxide (\( \ce{C6H5ONa} \)) and hydrogen gas, showcasing its acidic nature.

qns_content.text: Which compound results when 2-methylbutan-2-ol is dehydrated with conc. \( \ce{H2SO4} \)?

text_solutions: 2-Methylbutan-2-ol (\( \ce{CH3C(OH)(CH3)CH2CH3} \)) dehydrates to 2-methylbut-2-ene (\( \ce{CH3C(CH3)=CHCH3} \)) as the major product, following Saytzeff’s rule.

qns_content.text: What is the IUPAC name of \( \ce{CH3-CH(OH)-CH2-CH(OH)-CH3} \)?

text_solutions: The compound has a 5-carbon chain with -OH groups on carbons 2 and 4, named pentane-2,4-diol in IUPAC nomenclature.

qns_content.text: Which compound is produced when phenol is heated with zinc dust?

text_solutions: Phenol (\( \ce{C6H5OH} \)) is reduced to benzene (\( \ce{C6H6} \)) when heated with zinc dust, removing the -OH group as \( \ce{ZnO} \) and \( \ce{H2} \).

qns_content.text: Which of the following alcohols reacts fastest with Lucas reagent?

text_solutions: Lucas reagent (\( \ce{ZnCl2} \) in conc. \( \ce{HCl} \)) reacts fastest with tertiary alcohols like \( \ce{(CH3)3COH} \) due to the stability of the tertiary carbocation, causing immediate turbidity.

qns_content.text: What gas is evolved when phenol reacts with sodium metal?

text_solutions: Phenol (\( \ce{C6H5OH} \)) reacts with \( \ce{Na} \) to form sodium phenoxide and releases hydrogen gas (\( \ce{H2} \)), indicating its acidic nature.

qns_content.text: Why does ethane-1,2-diol have a higher boiling point than ethanol?

text_solutions: Ethane-1,2-diol (\( \ce{CH2OH-CH2OH} \)) has two -OH groups, leading to more extensive hydrogen bonding than ethanol (\( \ce{CH3CH2OH} \)), which has one -OH group, increasing its boiling point.

qns_content.text: Which alcohol is produced when ethyl magnesium bromide reacts with acetaldehyde followed by hydrolysis?

text_solutions: Ethyl magnesium bromide (\( \ce{CH3CH2MgBr} \)) reacts with acetaldehyde (\( \ce{CH3CHO} \)), adding the ethyl group to the carbonyl, yielding butan-2-ol (\( \ce{CH3CH(OH)CH2CH3} \)) after hydrolysis.

qns_content.text: What is the product when benzyl alcohol is oxidized with PCC?

text_solutions: Benzyl alcohol (\( \ce{C6H5CH2OH} \)), a primary alcohol, is oxidized to benzaldehyde (\( \ce{C6H5CHO} \)) with PCC, which stops at the aldehyde stage.

qns_content.text: What is the IUPAC name of \( \ce{CH3-CH(OH)-CH(OH)-CH3} \)?

text_solutions: The compound has a 4-carbon chain with -OH groups on carbons 2 and 3, named butane-2,3-diol in IUPAC nomenclature.

qns_content.text: Which phenol derivative has the highest acidity among the following?

text_solutions: 2,4,6-Trinitrophenol (picric acid) is the most acidic due to three electron-withdrawing -NO₂ groups stabilizing the phenoxide ion via resonance and inductive effects.

qns_content.text: Why is ortho-nitrophenol more acidic than ortho-methoxyphenol?

text_solutions: The -NO₂ group is electron-withdrawing, stabilizing the phenoxide ion via resonance and inductive effects, increasing acidity. The -OCH₃ group is electron-donating, reducing acidity.

qns_content.text: Which phenol derivative is steam volatile?

text_solutions: 2-Nitrophenol is steam volatile due to intramolecular hydrogen bonding between -OH and -NO₂, reducing intermolecular forces, unlike 4-nitrophenol.

qns_content.text: Which alcohol is produced by the reduction of propanal with \( \ce{NaBH4} \)?

text_solutions: Propanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CHO} \)) is reduced to propan-1-ol (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2OH} \)), a primary alcohol, using \( \ce{NaBH4} \), which reduces aldehydes to alcohols.

qns_content.text: What is the product when phenol reacts with \( \ce{CHCl3} \) and \( \ce{NaOH} \)?

text_solutions: In the Reimer-Tiemann reaction, phenol reacts with \( \ce{CHCl3} \) and \( \ce{NaOH} \) to form salicylaldehyde (2-hydroxybenzaldehyde) after acidification.

qns_content.text: Which compound is formed when phenol reacts with \( \ce{Br2} \) in water at room temperature?

text_solutions: Phenol reacts with \( \ce{Br2} \) in water to form 2,4,6-tribromophenol due to the strong activation of the ring by the -OH group, leading to trisubstitution.

qns_content.text: What is the product when 1-phenylethanol is oxidized with \( \ce{KMnO4} \)?

text_solutions: 1-Phenylethanol (\( \ce{C6H5CH(OH)CH3} \)), a secondary alcohol, is oxidized to acetophenone (\( \ce{C6H5COCH3} \)) with \( \ce{KMnO4} \), stopping at the ketone stage.

qns_content.text: What is the common name of \( \ce{CH3-CH(OH)-CH2-OH} \)?

text_solutions: \( \ce{CH3-CH(OH)-CH2-OH} \) (propane-1,2-diol) is a 3-carbon diol, commonly known as propylene glycol.

qns_content.text: What is the key factor that makes ortho-nitrophenol more acidic than phenol?

text_solutions: The -NO₂ group in ortho-nitrophenol exerts a strong electron-withdrawing effect, stabilizing the phenoxide ion and increasing acidity compared to phenol.

qns_content.text: Which compound is formed when butan-1-ol is oxidized with \( \ce{KMnO4} \)?

text_solutions: Butan-1-ol (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2OH} \)), a primary alcohol, is oxidized to butanoic acid (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2COOH} \)) with \( \ce{KMnO4} \), a strong oxidant.

qns_content.text: Which alcohol is produced by the hydroboration-oxidation of 1-pentene?

text_solutions: 1-Pentene (\( \ce{CH2=CH-CH2CH2CH3} \)) undergoes hydroboration-oxidation with \( \ce{BH3} \) and \( \ce{H2O2} \), adding -OH anti-Markovnikov to form pentan-1-ol (\( \ce{CH3(CH2)3CH2OH} \)).

qns_content.text: Which alcohol can be prepared from an alkene using \( \ce{BH3} \) followed by \( \ce{H2O2} \) and \( \ce{OH-} \)?

text_solutions: Hydroboration-oxidation of propene (\( \ce{CH3-CH=CH2} \)) follows anti-Markovnikov addition, yielding propan-1-ol (\( \ce{CH3-CH2-CH2OH} \)).

qns_content.text: Which compound is formed when propan-1-ol is oxidized with \( \ce{KMnO4} \)?

text_solutions: Propan-1-ol (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2OH} \)), a primary alcohol, is oxidized to propanoic acid (\( \ce{CH3CH2COOH} \)) with \( \ce{KMnO4} \), a strong oxidizing agent.

qns_content.text: Which compound is formed when phenol reacts with \( \ce{NaOH} \)?

text_solutions: Phenol (\( \ce{C6H5OH} \)) reacts with \( \ce{NaOH} \) to form sodium phenoxide (\( \ce{C6H5ONa} \)), demonstrating its acidic nature.

qns_content.text: What is the product when pentan-3-ol is dehydrated with conc. \( \ce{H2SO4} \)?

text_solutions: Pentan-3-ol (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH(OH)CH2CH3} \)) dehydrates to pent-2-ene (\( \ce{CH3CH=CHCH2CH3} \)) as the major product with conc. \( \ce{H2SO4} \), following Saytzeff’s rule.

qns_content.text: Which products are formed when phenol reacts with dilute \( \ce{HNO3} \)?

text_solutions: Phenol reacts with dilute \( \ce{HNO3} \) to form a mixture of o-nitrophenol and p-nitrophenol due to the ortho-para directing effect of the -OH group.

qns_content.text: What is the IUPAC name of glycerol?

text_solutions: Glycerol (\( \ce{HO-CH2-CH(OH)-CH2-OH} \)) has a 3-carbon chain with -OH groups on all three carbons, named propane-1,2,3-triol in IUPAC nomenclature.

qns_content.text: Which alcohol specifically yields pentan-3-one on oxidation with PCC?

text_solutions: Pentan-3-ol (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH(OH)CH2CH3} \)), a secondary alcohol, oxidizes to pentan-3-one (\( \ce{CH3CH2COCH2CH3} \)) with PCC.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a primary alcohol?

text_solutions: A primary alcohol has the -OH group attached to a carbon bonded to only one other carbon. \( \ce{CH3CH2CH2OH} \) (propan-1-ol) is a primary alcohol.

qns_content.text: What is the intermediate formed during the dehydration of butan-2-ol to but-2-ene?

text_solutions: Dehydration of butan-2-ol (\( \ce{CH3CH(OH)CH2CH3} \)) with conc. \( \ce{H2SO4} \) proceeds via an E1 mechanism, forming a carbocation (\( \ce{CH3CH+CH2CH3} \)) as the intermediate.

qns_content.text: What is the common name of \( \ce{CH2=CH-CH2OH} \)?

text_solutions: \( \ce{CH2=CH-CH2OH} \) is a 3-carbon compound with a double bond and an -OH group, commonly known as allyl alcohol.

qns_content.text: Which alcohol is used as a fuel additive to increase octane rating?

text_solutions: Ethanol (\( \ce{CH3CH2OH} \)) is commonly used as a fuel additive (e.g., in gasoline) to improve the octane rating and reduce emissions.

qns_content.text: Which alcohol resists oxidation with \( \ce{KMnO4} \) due to its structure?

text_solutions: 2-Methylpropan-2-ol (\( \ce{(CH3)3COH} \)), a tertiary alcohol, resists oxidation with \( \ce{KMnO4} \) because it lacks an alpha hydrogen.

qns_content.text: What is the total number of hydroxyl groups in propane-1,2,3-triol?

text_solutions: Propane-1,2,3-triol (glycerol, \( \ce{CH2OH-CHOH-CH2OH} \)) has three -OH groups, as indicated by ‘triol’ in its name.

qns_content.text: Which alcohol is used as an antifreeze in automobile radiators?

text_solutions: Ethane-1,2-diol (\( \ce{CH2OH-CH2OH} \)), commonly called ethylene glycol, is widely used as an antifreeze due to its ability to lower the freezing point of water.

qns_content.text: What activates the benzene ring in phenol towards electrophilic substitution?

text_solutions: The -OH group donates electrons to the benzene ring via resonance, increasing electron density at ortho and para positions, thus activating it for electrophilic substitution.

qns_content.text: Which products are formed when phenol reacts with \( \ce{Br2} \) in \( \ce{CS2} \) at low temperature?

text_solutions: In a non-polar solvent like \( \ce{CS2} \), phenol undergoes controlled monobromination to form a mixture of o-bromophenol and p-bromophenol, with the para isomer being the major product.

qns_content.text: Which alcohol reacts with \( \ce{Na} \) to produce a gas that burns with a pop sound?

text_solutions: Methanol (\( \ce{CH3OH} \)) reacts with \( \ce{Na} \) to release \( \ce{H2} \) gas, which burns with a pop sound, due to its acidic hydrogen.

qns_content.text: Which reagent is used to oxidize a secondary alcohol to a ketone?

text_solutions: PCC oxidizes secondary alcohols to ketones without further oxidation, unlike strong oxidants like \( \ce{KMnO4} \).

qns_content.text: Which alcohol produces a compound with a \( \ce{CH3CO-} \) group on oxidation that reacts with \( \ce{I2} \) and \( \ce{NaOH} \)?

text_solutions: Pentan-2-ol (\( \ce{CH3CH(OH)CH2CH2CH3} \)) oxidizes to pentan-2-one (\( \ce{CH3COCH2CH2CH3} \)), which has a \( \ce{CH3CO-} \) group and gives a positive iodoform test.

qns_content.text: Which reagent is used to synthesize pentan-2-ol from pent-1-ene?

text_solutions: Pent-1-ene (\( \ce{CH2=CHCH2CH2CH3} \)) reacts with \( \ce{H2SO4} \) and \( \ce{H2O} \) via acid-catalyzed hydration, adding -OH to the second carbon (Markovnikov’s rule) to form pentan-2-ol.

qns_content.text: Which reagent oxidizes propan-1-ol to propanal?

text_solutions: Propan-1-ol (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2OH} \)), a primary alcohol, is oxidized to propanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CHO} \)) with PCC, which stops at the aldehyde stage.

qns_content.text: Why is phenol soluble in \( \ce{NaOH} \) while ethanol is not?

text_solutions: Phenol is more acidic due to resonance stabilization of the phenoxide ion, allowing it to form a soluble salt with \( \ce{NaOH} \), unlike ethanol, which is a weaker acid.

qns_content.text: Which of the following alcohols is classified as a secondary alcohol?

text_solutions: A secondary alcohol has the -OH group attached to a carbon bonded to two other carbons. \( \ce{CH3-CH(OH)-CH3} \) (propan-2-ol) fits this definition.

qns_content.text: What is the product when phenol is heated with zinc dust?

text_solutions: Phenol (\( \ce{C6H5OH} \)) is reduced to benzene (\( \ce{C6H6} \)) when heated with zinc dust, which removes the -OH group as \( \ce{ZnO} \) and \( \ce{H2} \).

qns_content.text: Which compound results from the Kolbe’s reaction of phenol?

text_solutions: In Kolbe’s reaction, phenol reacts with \( \ce{CO2} \) under basic conditions followed by acidification to form salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid).

qns_content.text: What is the product when 2-methylpropan-2-ol is oxidized with \( \ce{KMnO4} \)?

text_solutions: 2-Methylpropan-2-ol (\( \ce{(CH3)3COH} \)), a tertiary alcohol, does not oxidize with \( \ce{KMnO4} \) due to the absence of an alpha hydrogen, so it remains unchanged.

qns_content.text: Which compound is produced when phenol is heated with \( \ce{CO2} \) and \( \ce{NaOH} \) at 125°C and 6 atm?

text_solutions: In Kolbe’s reaction, phenol reacts with \( \ce{CO2} \) and \( \ce{NaOH} \) under heat and pressure, followed by acidification, to form salicylic acid.

qns_content.text: How is 1-phenylethanol synthesized from a suitable alkene?

text_solutions: Styrene (\( \ce{CH2=CH-C6H5} \)) undergoes acid-catalyzed hydration with \( \ce{H2SO4} \) and \( \ce{H2O} \), adding -OH to the more substituted carbon (Markovnikov addition), forming 1-phenylethanol.

qns_content.text: What is the product when phenol reacts with concentrated \( \ce{H2SO4} \) at 100°C?

text_solutions: Phenol reacts with conc. \( \ce{H2SO4} \) at 100°C to form phenol-4-sulfonic acid (4-hydroxybenzenesulfonic acid) via electrophilic substitution at the para position.

qns_content.text: What is the product when pentan-2-ol is oxidized with PCC?

text_solutions: Pentan-2-ol (\( \ce{CH3CH(OH)CH2CH2CH3} \)), a secondary alcohol, is oxidized to pentan-2-one (\( \ce{CH3COCH2CH2CH3} \)) with PCC.

qns_content.text: What is the IUPAC name of the compound \( \ce{CH3-CH2-CH(OH)-CH3} \)?

text_solutions: The longest chain with the -OH group has 4 carbons, named butane. The -OH is on the second carbon from the end nearest to it, so it is butan-2-ol.

qns_content.text: Which reaction condition converts 2-methylpropan-2-ol to an alkene fastest?

text_solutions: Conc. \( \ce{H2SO4} \) at 140°C rapidly dehydrates 2-methylpropan-2-ol, a tertiary alcohol, to 2-methylpropene via a stable tertiary carbocation in an E1 mechanism.

qns_content.text: The dehydration of 2-methylpropan-2-ol with conc. \( \ce{H2SO4} \) follows which mechanism?

text_solutions: 2-Methylpropan-2-ol, a tertiary alcohol, dehydrates via an E1 mechanism with conc. \( \ce{H2SO4} \), forming a stable tertiary carbocation intermediate.

qns_content.text: Which alcohol is produced when propyl magnesium bromide reacts with formaldehyde followed by hydrolysis?

text_solutions: Propyl magnesium bromide (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2MgBr} \)) reacts with formaldehyde (\( \ce{HCHO} \)), adding the propyl group to the carbonyl, yielding butan-1-ol (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2OH} \)) after hydrolysis.

qns_content.text: Why does glycerol have a higher boiling point than ethanol?

text_solutions: Glycerol (\( \ce{CH2OH-CHOH-CH2OH} \)) has three -OH groups, forming extensive hydrogen bonding, which increases its boiling point compared to ethanol with one -OH group.

qns_content.text: Which alcohol is a trihydric alcohol?

text_solutions: A trihydric alcohol has three -OH groups. Glycerol (\( \ce{CH2OH-CHOH-CH2OH} \)) is a trihydric alcohol, also known as propane-1,2,3-triol.

qns_content.text: Which alcohol is a common ingredient in antifreeze and hydraulic fluids?

text_solutions: Ethane-1,2-diol (\( \ce{CH2OH-CH2OH} \)), or ethylene glycol, is widely used in antifreeze and hydraulic fluids due to its low freezing point and high boiling point.

qns_content.text: Why does 2-nitrophenol have a lower boiling point than 4-nitrophenol?

text_solutions: 2-Nitrophenol has intramolecular hydrogen bonding, reducing intermolecular forces and lowering its boiling point, while 4-nitrophenol has intermolecular hydrogen bonding, increasing its boiling point.

qns_content.text: What is the IUPAC name of \( \ce{CH2OH-CH2-CH2-OH} \)?

text_solutions: The compound has a 3-carbon chain with -OH groups on carbons 1 and 3, named propane-1,3-diol in IUPAC nomenclature.

qns_content.text: What is the total number of carbon atoms in \( \ce{CH3-CH(OH)-CH2-CH(OH)-CH3} \)?

text_solutions: Pentane-2,4-diol (\( \ce{CH3-CH(OH)-CH2-CH(OH)-CH3} \)) has a 5-carbon chain, as counted from one end to the other: \( \ce{CH3-CH-CH2-CH-CH3} \).

qns_content.text: Why is 4-nitrophenol less volatile than 2-nitrophenol?

text_solutions: 4-Nitrophenol has intermolecular hydrogen bonding, increasing intermolecular forces and reducing volatility, while 2-nitrophenol has intramolecular hydrogen bonding, making it more volatile.

qns_content.text: Which alcohol gives a positive iodoform test?

text_solutions: The iodoform test is positive for alcohols with a \( \ce{CH3CH(OH)-} \) group. Propan-2-ol (\( \ce{CH3CH(OH)CH3} \)) oxidizes to acetone, which gives a positive result.

qns_content.text: What is the IUPAC name of \( \ce{CH3-CH(OH)-CH2-OH} \)?

text_solutions: The compound has a 3-carbon chain with -OH groups on carbons 1 and 2, named propane-1,2-diol in IUPAC nomenclature.

qns_content.text: Which compound is formed when butan-2-ol is oxidized with PCC?

text_solutions: Butan-2-ol (\( \ce{CH3CH(OH)CH2CH3} \)), a secondary alcohol, is oxidized to butan-2-one (\( \ce{CH3COCH2CH3} \)) with PCC.

qns_content.text: Which condition favors mononitration of phenol when it reacts with \( \ce{HNO3} \)?

text_solutions: Dilute \( \ce{HNO3} \) at low temperature favors mononitration of phenol, producing a mixture of 2-nitrophenol and 4-nitrophenol, with the para isomer being the major product due to lower steric hindrance.

qns_content.text: Which alcohol forms a yellow precipitate with \( \ce{I2} \) and \( \ce{NaOH} \) only after oxidation?

text_solutions: Ethanol (\( \ce{CH3CH2OH} \)) oxidizes to acetaldehyde, which has a \( \ce{CH3CO-} \) group and gives a yellow iodoform precipitate with \( \ce{I2} \) and \( \ce{NaOH} \).

qns_content.text: What is the IUPAC name of \( \ce{HO-CH2-CH2-OH} \)?

text_solutions: The compound has a 2-carbon chain with -OH groups on both carbons. The base name is ethane, and with two -OH groups, it is ethane-1,2-diol.

qns_content.text: Which of the following alcohols does not give a positive iodoform test?

text_solutions: The iodoform test is positive for \( \ce{CH3CH(OH)-} \) structures. Propan-1-ol (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2OH} \)) oxidizes to propanal, which lacks the required group, giving a negative result.

qns_content.text: Which alcohol, on oxidation with PCC, yields a compound that does not react with \( \ce{I2} \) and \( \ce{NaOH} \)?

text_solutions: Propan-1-ol (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2OH} \)) oxidizes to propanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CHO} \)) with PCC, which lacks the \( \ce{CH3CO-} \) group and does not give an iodoform reaction.

qns_content.text: Which type of alcohol is commonly used in the manufacture of detergents?

text_solutions: Long-chain (fatty) alcohols such as lauryl alcohol are commonly used in the manufacture of detergents due to their ability to form surfactants.

qns_content.text: Which compound reacts with \( \ce{CH3MgBr} \) followed by hydrolysis to form a tertiary alcohol?

text_solutions: Propan-2-one (\( \ce{CH3COCH3} \)) reacts with \( \ce{CH3MgBr} \), adding a methyl group to the carbonyl carbon, yielding 2-methylpropan-2-ol (\( \ce{(CH3)3COH} \)) after hydrolysis, which is a tertiary alcohol.

qns_content.text: Which alcohol is used as a disinfectant in medical applications?

text_solutions: Propan-2-ol (\( \ce{CH3CH(OH)CH3} \)), commonly known as isopropyl alcohol, is widely used as a disinfectant due to its antiseptic properties.

qns_content.text: What is the product when phenol reacts with conc. \( \ce{H2SO4} \) at 25°C?

text_solutions: Phenol reacts with conc. \( \ce{H2SO4} \) at 25°C to form phenol-2-sulfonic acid (2-hydroxybenzenesulfonic acid) as the major product due to ortho substitution.

qns_content.text: Which reagent converts ethanol to acetaldehyde?

text_solutions: Ethanol (\( \ce{CH3CH2OH} \)), a primary alcohol, is oxidized to acetaldehyde (\( \ce{CH3CHO} \)) with PCC, which selectively oxidizes to the aldehyde stage.

qns_content.text: Which reagent converts pentan-1-ol to pentanoic acid?

text_solutions: Pentan-1-ol (\( \ce{CH3(CH2)3CH2OH} \)), a primary alcohol, is oxidized to pentanoic acid (\( \ce{CH3(CH2)3COOH} \)) using a strong oxidizing agent like \( \ce{KMnO4} \).

qns_content.text: Which reaction demonstrates the acidic nature of phenol?

text_solutions: Phenol reacts with \( \ce{NaOH} \) to form sodium phenoxide (\( \ce{C6H5ONa} \)) and water, indicating its acidic nature due to the stabilization of the phenoxide ion by resonance.

qns_content.text: Which of the following alcohols gives a negative iodoform test?

text_solutions: Butan-1-ol (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2OH} \)) oxidizes to butanal, which lacks the \( \ce{CH3CO-} \) or \( \ce{CH3CH(OH)-} \) structure, giving a negative iodoform test.

qns_content.text: What is the common name of \( \ce{CH2OH-CHOH-CH2OH} \)?

text_solutions: \( \ce{CH2OH-CHOH-CH2OH} \) is a trihydric alcohol with three -OH groups on a 3-carbon chain, commonly known as glycerol.

qns_content.text: Which alcohol is produced when methyl magnesium bromide reacts with propanal followed by hydrolysis?

text_solutions: Methyl magnesium bromide (\( \ce{CH3MgBr} \)) reacts with propanal (\( \ce{CH3CH2CHO} \)), adding the methyl group to the carbonyl, yielding butan-2-ol (\( \ce{CH3CH(OH)CH2CH3} \)) after hydrolysis.

qns_content.text: Which compound is oxidized in air to form colored quinones?

text_solutions: Phenol (\( \ce{C6H5OH} \)) undergoes oxidation in air to form quinones and other colored compounds, which may impart a yellowish or brownish color.

qns_content.text: Which reagent dehydrates propan-2-ol to propene?

text_solutions: Propan-2-ol (\( \ce{CH3CH(OH)CH3} \)) is dehydrated to propene (\( \ce{CH3CH=CH2} \)) using concentrated \( \ce{H2SO4} \) at 170°C, following an E1 mechanism.

qns_content.text: Which alcohol is produced when 1-butene reacts with \( \ce{BH3} \) followed by \( \ce{H2O2} \) and \( \ce{OH-} \)?

text_solutions: 1-Butene (\( \ce{CH2=CHCH2CH3} \)) undergoes hydroboration-oxidation, adding -OH anti-Markovnikov to form butan-1-ol (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH2CH2OH} \)).

qns_content.text: What is the product when pentan-3-ol is oxidized with PCC?

text_solutions: Pentan-3-ol (\( \ce{CH3CH2CH(OH)CH2CH3} \)), a secondary alcohol, is oxidized to pentan-3-one (\( \ce{CH3CH2COCH2CH3} \)) with PCC.

qns_content.text: What is the IUPAC name of \( \ce{CH3-C(OH)(CH3)-CH3} \)?

text_solutions: The longest chain is propane with two methyl groups on the second carbon, where the -OH is attached, named 2-methylpropan-2-ol.
